candidates.name: d1r1A
candidates.idea: Test a wider name column while retaining enough room for the complete alpha identifiers before their natural break at code. Keep subdivision links and the Independent header whole; use the remaining space for the numeric column.
candidates.label: gold

whys: Names and identifiers remain whole, and compact, uniform rows make lookup and comparison easy. The code headers wrap naturally, though the narrow code columns make the header feel slightly tight.
Names and ISO links remain on one line, with compact, consistent rows that support scanning across codes. The paired alpha columns have matching widths; several headers wrap cleanly.

candidates.label: gold

whys: Whole names and identifiers and evenly spaced rows support quick lookup. The paired alpha columns are slightly tight, while the numeric column has a little more space than its content needs.

Names and links stay intact on single lines, and the compact, even rows make the codes easy to compare. The alpha columns match, and the slightly wider numeric column accommodates its header comfortably.

The body is compact and easy to scan, with complete names and identifiers on single lines. The alpha headers sit slightly tighter than in C, while the numeric column gains space that its short values do not need.

candidates.label: gold

whys: Names and identifiers stay on one line, with a clear, consistent row rhythm. The narrower name column still accommodates this sample, though the longest name has less breathing room.

candidates.name: contrast
candidates.idea: The near-equal widths give short codes excessive space while constraining country names and the ISO 3166-2 links. The 119 px link column leaves only 98 px for text, so the 134 px header cannot stay on one line and link identifiers may wrap.
candidates.label: bad

whys: All content fits, but the narrow name and link columns wrap names and split most ISO identifiers. Equal-width columns give short codes excessive space, while the single shorter body row interrupts the rhythm.
Equal-width columns leave little space for names and ISO links while giving short codes ample room. Several names wrap, nearly every link breaks across lines, and the resulting tall rows slow lookup.

Equal-looking columns leave the country names cramped and split most ISO identifiers across lines. The unusually short Anguilla row interrupts an otherwise tall row pattern, making comparisons harder.
Country names stay whole, but every ISO link identifier wraps across two lines. This makes rows much taller and leaves large areas of empty space around the short codes, slowing comparison.
Names remain on one line, but every ISO link splits at the hyphen, making the identifiers harder to read and producing tall rows with unused space in the other columns.

Country names remain whole and the rows are consistent, but every ISO identifier wraps after the hyphen. This separates each identifier into two lines and makes the table much taller, slowing lookup and comparison.

d1.purpose: Provide a compact reference for identifying countries and territories and their current ISO 3166-1 codes, subdivision-code links and independence status.
tasks: Look up a country or territory by English name and read across to its codes and status.
Find or compare alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes down their respective columns.
Follow a subdivision-code link for a selected entry.
Read the alphabetical list sequentially while keeping each entry's attributes associated with its name.
relations: Each row binds one name to its two letter codes, numeric code, subdivision-code link and independence status.
The alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric columns are parallel identifiers for the same entry; the subdivision link and independence status provide related information.
roles: The header labels six distinct fields; its longer labels may use multiple lines.
The first column identifies entries and anchors row-by-row lookup.
The three code columns support scanning and comparison; the last two columns provide a link and a status.
keep_whole: Individual words in names and headers.
Alpha-2, alpha-3 and three-digit numeric codes, including leading zeros.
Subdivision-code link labels and the Independent header.
may_wrap: Multiword country and territory names at word spaces.
same_scale: The alpha-2 and alpha-3 columns should have equal or closely related widths because they serve parallel tasks.
The three code columns should read as a compact group; names and subdivision links warrant more space because their content is longer.
d1.h_vs_v: The viewport cannot accommodate every header and value on one line. Wrapping selected headers costs height once, while wrapping names can increase individual row heights throughout the table; preserving complete subdivision links and compact codes makes cross-row scanning more reliable.

d2.purpose: Provide a compact reference for the current ISO 3166-1 codes associated with each country or territory.
tasks: Find a country or territory by name and read across to its codes and status.
Compare alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes across entries.
relations: Each row connects one name with three identifiers, a subdivision-code link and an independence status.
The three code columns form a related group; the link and status supply distinct reference information.
roles: The first row labels the fields and may be taller than the data rows.
The first column identifies each entry and serves as the main lookup index.
The remaining columns contain short identifiers, links and status values for reading across rows.
keep_whole: Individual words in names and headers
Alpha and numeric codes, including leading zeros
may_wrap: Multiword country and territory names at natural word boundaries
same_scale: Alpha-2 and alpha-3 columns should have similar widths.
The numeric code column should remain visually related to the two alpha-code columns.
d2.h_vs_v: The viewport cannot accommodate every header and name on one line. Wrapping headers is inexpensive because it affects only one row; wrapping names costs more vertical space and can make scanning entries less even. Preserving complete links and codes supports reliable lookup.

d3.purpose: Provide a compact reference for the current ISO 3166-1 codes and related information for each listed country or territory.
tasks: Find a country or territory by name and read across to its codes and independence status.
Compare alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes across entries.
Locate the corresponding ISO 3166-2 subdivision-code link.
relations: Each row associates one English short name with its alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes, subdivision-code link and independence status.
The three code columns are parallel identifiers for the same entity; the ISO 3166-2 link points to related subdivision information.
roles: The first column acts as the lookup key even though no row headers are declared.
The header row names the six fields; the remaining rows are individual country or territory records.
The independence column is a status field, while the ISO 3166-2 column is a navigation field.
keep_whole: Each alpha-2, alpha-3 and three-digit numeric code, including leading zeros.
Individual words in country names and headers.
Each ISO 3166-2 link label if space permits; otherwise preserve its meaningful identifier components.
may_wrap: ISO 3166-2 link labels at available punctuation break opportunities when necessary.
same_scale: The alpha-2 and alpha-3 columns should have similar widths because they have parallel roles and similarly short values.
The numeric code column should remain visually comparable to the alphabetic code columns.
The name and link columns merit more room than the short-code columns when that keeps useful lookup text together.
d3.h_vs_v: The 719px limit makes some header wrapping necessary. Wider names and links preserve continuous row scanning, while narrower versions make room for clearer headers at the cost of taller rows.

analysis.strengths: All content is visible, country names and identifiers remain on one line, and the paired alpha columns have equal widths. The table leaves 18 px of viewport space unused.
analysis.faults: The longest country name has less breathing room than in the other layouts, and the numeric header sits fairly close to its right border.
analysis.spatial_logic: Keeps the table compact while allocating enough width to preserve every body row on one line and both long right-hand headers intact.

analysis.strengths: Preserves the clean, single-line body rows and equal alpha columns. It gives the numeric header more room than P.
analysis.faults: Uses the full viewport without changing any line breaks or row heights; the extra width has limited practical effect for these 14 rows.
analysis.spatial_logic: Spends P’s remaining width on the country-name and numeric columns, while retaining the widths of the paired alpha columns and the two rightmost columns.

analysis.strengths: Gives the country names the most room, preserves equal alpha columns, and leaves the numeric header comfortable.
analysis.faults: The alpha headers are the tightest of the four layouts, while the extra country-name width does not prevent any wrapping in this particular set of rows.
analysis.spatial_logic: Transfers 5 px from each alpha column to the country-name column relative to Q, keeping the numeric and right-hand columns unchanged.

analysis.strengths: Combines the wider country-name column of R with slightly more room for the paired alpha headers. Every body entry stays on one line.
analysis.faults: The numeric header has less space than in Q or R, and the extra country-name width produces no change in line breaks for the displayed rows.
analysis.spatial_logic: Balances R’s generous name column against the three code columns by taking 4 px from the numeric column and giving 2 px to each alpha column.

rounds.insights: All four layouts fit and preserve the same reading structure: a two-line header, single-line body entries, and aligned code columns. The meaningful trade-off is between a compact table and a little more breathing room around the country names and code headers; using all 720 px does not itself improve the displayed content. Equal widths for the alpha columns help readers compare the related codes, while the wider link column keeps its identifiers intact.

contrast.why: The near-equal widths give short codes excessive space while constraining country names and the ISO 3166-2 links. The 119 px link column leaves only 98 px for text, so the 134 px header cannot stay on one line and link identifiers may wrap.

sameFunctionGroups.why: These columns contain parallel country identifiers used for lookup and comparison. Similar widths support their shared role, while a slightly wider numeric column accommodates its longer header.

synthesis.rationale: S keeps every body entry on one line and gives the country names comfortable room, including Antigua and Barbuda. Its two alpha-code columns share a width, with a modest allowance for the longer numeric header. Q, R and P preserve the same readable breaks and row heights, but their small width differences do not make them distinct enough to submit as additional finalists.

general: Protect complete identifiers and natural word breaks before optimizing density.
Give parallel fields a consistent visual scale while allowing for meaningful differences in content.
Allocate space to lookup labels and long entries according to their needs, rather than distributing width equally.
specific: A 155 px ISO 3166-2 column keeps its header and visible link values on one line.
The 112 px independence column accommodates its unbroken header.
All four candidates fit the viewport and have the same row heights.

synthesis.tradeoffs: S uses the full available width and gives the name column more room than Q or P; Q gives the code columns slightly more room. P leaves 18 px unused while retaining the same line breaks, and R gives the numeric column more space at the expense of the alpha columns.
synthesis.uncertain: The candidates are very close visually, and the preference for S is modest. The contrast layout has not been rendered, so the exact breaks in its link values are uncertain.

critique.good: All entries and subdivision links remain on one line, and the uniform rows make the list easy to scan across and down. The parallel alpha columns have matching widths and natural header breaks.
critique.problems: The table is well balanced, though the longest name has relatively little spare space. The status column has considerable empty space in its body, but its width is needed by the header.
critique.cause: The 190px name column accommodates the longest displayed name; the 112px status column is set by the unbroken Independent header.

critique.good: The alpha headers break naturally and the code columns have comfortable spacing. Links and status remain easy to read.
critique.problems: Antigua and Barbuda wraps, creating one taller row and interrupting the otherwise even rhythm. The extra code-column space provides little benefit for the short values.
critique.cause: The 160px name column is too narrow for that name, while the 96px, 96px and 100px code columns consume space that could support names.

critique.good: The wide name column gives entries ample room, and all body rows remain uniform. The compact code group keeps related identifiers close together.
critique.problems: Both alpha headers split their identifiers after the hyphen, making Alpha-2 and Alpha-3 harder to read as complete labels. The extra name-column space is largely unused by these entries.
critique.cause: The 74px alpha columns are too narrow for the complete Alpha-2 and Alpha-3 labels, while the 220px name column takes more space than this list needs.

critique.good: All content fits, with unbroken names, identifiers and links. The equal alpha-code columns form a compact group, the first column has comfortable room for lookup, and the consistent body row heights make scanning easy.
critique.problems: The four wrapped headers create a relatively tall header row, but their breaks are natural and the hierarchy remains clear.
critique.cause: The 82px alpha columns and 88px numeric column wrap their headers; the 200px name column wraps its longer header.

critique.good: All content fits without broken words, and the equal alpha-code columns support comparison. Body rows remain uniform and easy to scan.
critique.problems: The extra space in the alpha-code columns does not change their header wrapping or improve the short values. The name column is slightly tighter around the longest name.
critique.cause: The alpha columns are 88px each, while the name column is reduced to 190px.

critique.good: All names, codes and links remain on one line. Even row heights make scanning and reading across straightforward. The code headers wrap naturally, keeping Alpha-2 and Alpha-3 intact.
critique.problems: The link and status columns have little spare space, while the first column has enough room for the displayed names but limited room for longer ones.
critique.cause: The 190px name column balances the 85px and 92px code columns; the 155px link and 112px status columns are close to their measured one-line needs.

critique.good: The code columns are spacious, and identifiers and links remain intact.
critique.problems: The first header takes three lines, and Antigua and Barbuda wraps, interrupting the otherwise even row rhythm. The extra code-column space provides little benefit for the short values.
critique.cause: The 145px name column is too narrow for the longest displayed name, while the 100px, 100px and 107px code columns consume space that would be more useful for names.

critique.good: The generous name column keeps all displayed entries on one line, with even data rows and intact links and values.
critique.problems: The Alpha-2 and Alpha-3 headers break after the hyphen, separating each label from its distinguishing number and making the code group harder to scan.
critique.cause: The 75px alpha columns are too narrow to keep each complete Alpha-2 or Alpha-3 label together. The 220px name column takes space beyond what the displayed names need.

critique.good: All entries, codes and links are visible on one line, with uniform data-row heights. The two alpha-code columns match, and the header breaks are natural.
critique.problems: The name column has more room than these entries need, while the three code columns are somewhat uneven in width.
critique.cause: The 200px name column is wider than required for the longest displayed name; the numeric column is 12px wider than each 80px alpha column.

critique.good: All content remains visible, with single-line data rows and natural header breaks. The code columns are more closely matched in width.
critique.problems: The name column has less breathing room than in d2r1A, without changing the table height or wrapping. The numeric column is still slightly wider than the alpha columns.
critique.cause: Moving 10px from the name column to the alpha columns reduces the width difference within the code group, but does not produce a meaningful change in readability.

critique.good: All entries and subdivision links stay on one line, giving the table a compact, even rhythm and making rows easy to scan. The parallel code columns have equal widths, and all three codes remain intact.
critique.problems: The alpha headers break after the hyphen, separating each digit from its label. The name column has more space than these 14 entries need, while the code headers feel cramped.
critique.cause: The 70px alpha columns leave only 49px for text; the 220px name column has room to give up.

critique.good: Alpha-2 and Alpha-3 each stay together in their headers, and the full subdivision links remain easy to read. The code columns have a comfortable, consistent scale.
critique.problems: The name header takes three lines, and Antigua and Barbuda wraps, interrupting the otherwise regular body rows. The narrow lookup column feels constricted beside the generous code columns.
critique.cause: The 150px name column trades too much space for the 95px alpha columns and 100px numeric column.

critique.good: Country names and short codes remain intact, and the code headers break at natural spaces. The name column has a comfortable width.
critique.problems: Every subdivision link breaks within its identifier, making every body row twice as tall and weakening continuous scanning. The repeated empty space in the other columns gives the table a loose, unbalanced rhythm.
critique.cause: The 111px link column is too narrow for the link labels; the 98px alpha columns and 100px numeric column consume space that would be more useful there.

critique.good: All entries and identifiers remain on one line, and the table fits the viewport. The parallel code columns have comparable widths, with clean header breaks after Alpha-2, Alpha-3 and Numeric. The name header also breaks naturally before its parenthetical qualifier.
critique.problems: The table leaves some unused space at the right, but the content does not need it.
critique.cause: The 182px name column accommodates all displayed names; the 85px alphabetic code columns and 82px numeric column preserve their header units. The 155px link and 112px status columns keep their content whole.

critique.good: All body entries remain on one line, and the table fits the viewport. The link and status fields are clear and easy to scan.
critique.problems: Both alphabetic code headers break after the hyphen, separating Alpha from its distinguishing number. The wider name column adds empty space without improving the displayed rows.
critique.cause: The 70px alpha columns are too narrow to keep Alpha-2 and Alpha-3 together, while the 220px name column exceeds the width needed for these entries.
